subject: Clarifying subprocessor access patterns and TIA scope for Zenity pilot
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@zenityhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding — data routing & subprocessors questions

Hi Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we start the onboarding paperwork for the EU pilot, legal has a couple of focused questions so we can scope a TIA and confirm whether the standard SCCs + UK addendum cover Zenity's telemetry and event payloads. Specifically: 

1) Can you provide a breakdown of which subprocessors touch raw patient-identifiable payloads vs. aggregated telemetry? We need roles and countries of processing.
2) For KV cache / prefix caching — are caches material persisted outside the region for >24 hours? If yes, what safeguards apply?
3) If we require UK IDTA addendum for UK-resident patient data, do you have a published playbook or example addendum text?

Legal suggested a short tech + privacy Q&A and a candidate scope for a TIA before they sign the DPA. Can you share a subprocessor matrix and a proposed TIA scope by EOD Tuesday?

If helpful, Tom (cc) will be our technical lead for the pilot.

Best,
Laura Chen
Head of Privacy Operations
Zenity Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@zenityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding — data routing & subprocessors questions

Laura —

Appreciate the clear list. Summary answers inline and attached is a current subprocessor matrix (attachment: redwood-subprocessor-matrix.csv). I also put a first-pass TIA scope at the bottom of this message.

1) Subprocessors & data categories: the matrix lists every subprocessor, processing activity, and locations. Short summary: our infra, logging and monitoring vendors (x-logging, y-metrics) only see aggregated telemetry; model-serving nodes and S3-like storage can see raw payloads for inference requests. All subprocessors that may access raw request payloads are listed and are either EU-hosted or covered by SCCs + Processor Addendum.

2) Cache persistence: our KV cache for active sessions is ephemeral by default and kept in-region for the Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted, short-lived backups may traverse a US-based cache for disaster recovery; default TTL is 6 hours and we can reduce or disable cross-region persistence for Zenity. We can add contractual language to restrict cross-border caching for the pilot.

3) UK IDTA/addendum: we do have a standard UK addendum template and a playbook for evidence (we use the UK IDTA text approved by legal). I can share the template — as a next step, we normally populate the fields for the customer-specific TIA and confirm any additional technical measures.

TIA scope (first-pass):
- Data types in scope: inference request payloads for EU/UK patients (PII + clinical attributes), logging/metrics (aggregated).
- Subprocessors in scope: model-serving nodes, object storage, on-call SRE monitoring.
- Technical safeguards: in-region key management, prefix-based caching disabled for cross-region, KV TTL <= 1 hour for pilot.
- Audit provisions: quarterly evidence handoff (logs of subprocessor access), SOC2 snapshot, and support for sample e-discovery on request.

Next step: propose a 30-minute technical + privacy session Wed/Thu; I can bring Kimberly on the call for deployment specifics and Marissa for contractual items. If that works I will share the UK addendum template and a short Drive folder with the TIA checklist.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-subprocessor-matrix.csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot onboarding — data routing & subprocessors questions

Jonas / Kim —

Looping you both in with a quick commercial note: Zenity is a strategic EU pilot and pricing/commitment will influence whether we offer the extra engineering work to adjust cache persistence defaults. If legal wants a contract clause to limit cross-border caching and in-region KMS, we should price the change and aim to include it in the pilot SOW rather than a perpetual commitment.

Kim — can you draft the SOW bullet that describes the in-region KMS + cache TTL change and include an estimated engineering lift (hours) for a one-month pilot?

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.inference>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@zenityhealth.com>
Cc: Tom Berger <t.berger@zenityhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2026 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding — data routing & subprocessors questions

Laura / Tom —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our internal alignment (cc Marissa + Kim), attached is a short TIA questionnaire we prepared to help Zenity legal scope the final TIA and UK addendum (attachment: zenity-tia-questions.docx). Key changes from our standard hosted defaults that we can contractually commit to for the pilot: 

- Disable cross-region prefix/KV caching for the Zenity pilot (all inference cache entries TTL <= 1 hour; persisted caches confined to EU region).
- Use customer-specific KMS in-region for encryption-at-rest for any persisted artifacts related to the pilot.
- Provide subprocessor access logs for the pilot on a bi-weekly cadence; include sample evidence for one month post-pilot.

SCCs & UK addendum: we will provide the standard SCCs + our UK addendum template. If Zenity requires an IDTA-style annex, legal can propose field-level edits and we will review. For the TIA, please confirm whether the scope should also include internal debug traces (these are off by default for the pilot; enable only on request).

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical + legal call Thurs 28 May 09:30 BST / 01:30 PDT — confirm?
2) Zenity returns the completed TIA questionnaire (attached) + any redlines to the UK addendum by EOD Mon 1 Jun.
3) We finalize the DPA addendum and SOW for the pilot; engineering implements cache/KMS config during sprint week 23.

Link to shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0AExZenity/TIA-notes 

If that timeline works, I will ask legal to send the UK addendum template and we will start SOW pricing.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
